messages:
Evan: Kicking off a quick smoke + sanity bench for lightning-7b on the 8xA10 pool. Can someone run a latency sweep and a short throughput pass? target: p95 < 120ms for 512 tokens, steady throughput >= 180 tok/s.

Priya: happy to take the latency sweep. will run short samples at 1k prompts (randomized lengths). ETA ~20m. @Sam can you queue the throughput job?

Sam: queued a 10m throughput run on warm kernels (batch sizes 1..8). job id: run-4821. I set max_seq=512, token_chunk=32. will post results when done.

Maya: quick note — please capture kv-cache warmup vs cold. we saw ~15% p95 improvement after one prompt in last model. if you can export cold/warm metrics that'd help rollout gating.

Evan: yes capture cold/warm. also include memory headroom and any OOMs. if results look good we can do a canary rollout to dedicated pool.

deploy-bot: CI: perf-checker started for run-4821 — collectors attached: latency-exporter, mem-sampler. correlating with kernel-version: 1.4.2

Sam: throughput run finished. summary (10m warm run):
```
run-4821 summary:
- avg tok/s: 195
- p50 latency (512): 62ms
- p95 latency (512): 118ms
- p99 latency (512): 210ms
- GPU mem used (max): 22.1GB
- kv-cache warmup delta: -12% p95
- errors: 0
```

Priya: latency sweep done (1k prompts, mixed lengths). summary:
- cold p95 (first-token): 145ms
- warm p95 (subsequent): 125ms
- end-to-end p95 w/ network sim (us-west->eu): 170ms

Maya: thanks. p95 warm 125ms is close to the 120ms bar but throughput looks fine. p99 tail 210ms is concerning for some low-latency routes. do we have traces for the p99 outliers?

Sam: attaching a small trace excerpt from the run — looks like a kernel fallback on some long sequences causing spike.
```
[trace id: t-77]
- t=0.0 conv dispatch
- t=0.9 kernel A exec
- t=1.8 fallback to kernel B (seq >= 480)
- t=2.7 token emit
```

Evan: ok that fallback explains p99. two options: 1) restrict max_seq to 480 in hosted config to avoid fallback, 2) land a kernel fix (longer lead time). For immediate rollout prefer option 1 + autoscale buffer.

Priya: will re-run a targeted sweep with max_seq=480 and post numbers. also can we run a quick cost delta for quantized vs fp16? curious if switching quantization profile changes latency.

Sam: did a quick smoke with max_seq=480 (5m warm):
```
- avg tok/s: 188
- p95 (480): 112ms
- p99 (480): 160ms
- mem max: 20.6GB
```

Maya: those numbers look fine. p95 now comfortably under 120ms. p99 improved but still higher for very long contexts — acceptable for initial canary if we gate by route.

Evan: proposed rollout plan:
- canary to 5% of hosted traffic (routes: low-latency non-critical paths) with max_seq=480
- monitor p95/p99, error rate, cost per token for 30m
- if stable -> 25% -> 100% over 2h with rollback thresholds (p95 > 130ms or error > 0.5%)

Priya: agreed. I'll create canary config and add KV-cache prewarm enabled.

Sam: canary config uploaded: cfg/lightning7b/canary-2025-03-15.yaml (includes max_seq=480, prewarm=true, quant=auto). dogfooding check: :thumbsup: 

Maya: I'll add eval monitors for the prompt-set 2025/latency-watch and alert if regression >5% on p95.

Evan: thanks team. follow-ups:
- Priya: post canary numbers here after 30m
- Sam: keep an eye on kernel fallback alarms
- Maya: publish eval/dashboard changes

Priya: canary started @ 1748123520, routing 5%. will update at 1748123720 (30m).

deploy-bot: Canary deployment lightning-7b -> hosted-canary (5%) started by Priya at 1748123520. rollout id: r-9007.

Sam: quick FYI — I saw a slight token-cost increase in quant=auto experiments (~3%). not huge but flagging.

Maya: noted. we'll track cost per completion in the console. if cost regresses >4% we auto-roll back.

Priya: canary 30m results:
- p95 (observed): 115ms
- p99: 162ms
- error rate: 0.02%
- avg tok/s: 180
- cost delta vs baseline: +2.6%

Evan: looks good to me. proceeding to 25% in 10m, then full roll in 2h if the trend holds. :rocket:

Sam: bumped to 25% at 1748123820. monitoring.

Maya: setting a watch on p95 and p99 dashboards + slack alerts to #incidents if thresholds breached.

Evan: perfect. we'll document the gated max_seq UX note in the onboarding checklist (so product teams know the default behavior). thanks all.
